headline: 40 years on: Argentina honors Diego Maradona ahead of Austria clash
summary: Fans and players remember the late icon's legendary 1986 World Cup performance as the reigning champions prepare for their second Group J match.
details: Argentina's players, coaching staff, and supporters are keeping the memory of Diego Maradona alive as they prepare to face Austria in their second World Cup Group J match in Dallas.

The match coincides with the 40th anniversary of Maradona's iconic performance against England in the 1986 World Cup quarter-finals, where he scored both the 'Hand of God' and the 'Goal of the Century'.
In Argentina, June 22 is commemorated as the Day of the Argentine Footballer to honor these historic achievements.
Maradona's influence remains immense, with fans in Kansas City and Texas displaying giant flags and banners linking him with Lionel Messi, describing their relationship as 'simbiosis'.
Coach Lionel Scaloni recalled his childhood memories of watching the 1986 goal on a small TV at his grandmother's house, admitting he would be emotional seeing the highlights again.
The connection to Austria is also notable, as Maradona once scored his only international hat-trick against them in a 5-1 victory back in 1980.
Diego Maradona passed away on November 25, 2020, at the age of 60, following a heart attack while recovering from brain surgery.
caption:
From the 'Hand of God' to the 'Goal of the Century'—Argentina remembers a legend.

Argentina's players, coaching staff, and supporters are keeping the memory of Diego Maradona alive as they prepare to face Austria in their second World Cup Group J match in Dallas.

The match coincides with the 40th anniversary of Maradona's iconic performance against England in the 1986 World Cup quarter-finals, where he scored both the 'Hand of God' and the 'Goal of the Century'.

In Argentina, June 22 is commemorated as the Day of the Argentine Footballer to honor these historic achievements.

Maradona's influence remains immense, with fans in Kansas City and Texas displaying giant flags and banners linking him with Lionel Messi, describing their relationship as 'simbiosis'.

Coach Lionel Scaloni recalled his childhood memories of watching the 1986 goal on a small TV at his grandmother's house, admitting he would be emotional seeing the highlights again.

The connection to Austria is also notable, as Maradona once scored his only international hat-trick against them in a 5-1 victory back in 1980.

Diego Maradona passed away on November 25, 2020, at the age of 60, following a heart attack while recovering from brain surgery.

#Argentina #Maradona #WorldCup #Football #Legend

Source: Prothom Alo, bdnews24.com, Somoy News

headline: Over $2bn in remittance inflows cross $2bn in 21 days of June
summary: Bangladesh Bank forecasts total annual remittances could reach $36 billion by the end of the fiscal year as inflows continue a strong upward trend.
details: Expatriates have sent over $2.08 billion in the first 21 days of June, marking a 4.7 percent increase compared to the same period last year.
If the current pace holds, June inflows are expected to exceed $3 billion, which would extend a streak of monthly inflows remaining above $3 billion for seven consecutive months.
Bangladesh Bank officials project that total remittances for the fiscal year could reach $36 billion, with inflows already standing at $34.84 billion as of June 21.
The central bank reports that overall inflows for the first 11 months and 21 days of the current fiscal year are up 18.1 percent year-on-year.
Executive Director Arief Hossain Khan noted that while seasonal factors like Eid-ul-Azha and Eid-ul-Fitr typically boost flows, the positive trend has continued even after the festivals.
On average, expatriates are sending $99.2 million per day in June, equivalent to approximately Tk 256.33 billion for the first 21 days.
Remittance inflows remain a critical pillar of the economy, helping to stabilize macroeconomic conditions and foreign exchange reserves.
As of Monday, gross reserves stood at $35.74 billion, while reserves under the BPM6 standard were $31.18 billion.
caption:
Over $2 billion sent in just 21 days! 💸

Bangladesh is seeing a massive surge in remittances as the fiscal year closes.

Expatriates have sent over $2.08 billion in the first 21 days of June, marking a 4.7 percent increase compared to the same period last year.

If the current pace holds, June inflows are expected to exceed $3 billion, which would extend a streak of monthly inflows remaining above $3 billion for seven consecutive months.

Bangladesh Bank officials project that total remittances for the fiscal year could reach $36 billion, with inflows already standing at $34.84 billion as of June 21.

The central bank reports that overall inflows for the first 11 months and 21 days of the current fiscal year are up 18.1 percent year-on-year.

Executive Director Arief Hossain Khan noted that while seasonal factors like Eid-ul-Azha and Eid-ul-Fitr typically boost flows, the positive trend has continued even after the festivals.

On average, expatriates are sending $99.2 million per day in June, equivalent to approximately Tk 256.33 billion for the first 21 days.

Remittance inflows remain a critical pillar of the economy, helping to stabilize macroeconomic conditions and foreign exchange reserves.

As of Monday, gross reserves stood at $35.74 billion, while reserves under the BPM6 standard were $31.18 billion.
